findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is set, so objects in this bucket are stored unencrypted by default (or only with default SSE-S3 depending on account settings), risking exposure of sensitive report data at rest.
No acl attribute or aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined, leaving the bucket subject to default/inherited ACLs and no explicit protection against public access.
Ledger export data (likely sensitive financial data) is stored without any server_side_encryption_configuration, exposing it to risk if the underlying storage or backups are compromised.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is associated with this bucket, so there is no explicit enforcement preventing public ACLs/policies from being applied later.
This bucket stores model artifacts but has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving data unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is configured, so there's no explicit safeguard against accidental public exposure of model artifacts.
Operational runbooks bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration, risking exposure of potentially sensitive operational data if storage is compromised.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricts public access for this bucket.

Despite having encryption and versioning configured, this bucket (used for log-delivery-write ACL) has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, leaving it without explicit protection against public exposure of audit logs.

This object is uploaded to the reports_archive bucket, which has no encryption configuration, and no server_side_encryption override is specified on the object itself, so the vendor roster file (potentially sensitive) is stored unencrypted.
